title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Mobile massage
audience: Mobile massage therapists who quote per session, per visit or per pack, and want a price that shows the travel, set-up and time that a home visit involves, without making health claims.
learningOutcomes: Write a mobile massage offer with a clear session length, time frame, client inputs and risk
Show the travel charge and the set-up time as visible lines rather than hidden extras
Price sessions and packs on value and cost, and keep every claim within what you can support

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: “I do massage” is a service. “A 60-minute massage at your home, starting with a check of what you want from the session, with the room set up and cleared before I arrive and a written note of the session afterwards” is an offer. The client buys the session, its length and the certainty that the visit will be organised and safe in their own space.

instruction.heading: The five parts of a mobile offer
instruction.body: Name the session in plain words. Give the length, including set-up, clean-down and the travel to the client. List what the client provides, such as a firm, level surface and a clear route to it. Add one certainty element, such as a check of the client’s wishes at the start and a written note afterwards. Set the risk you carry, such as the change of pressure or a shorter session if the client asks. Write the scope and exclusions down, because a written quote becomes binding once it is accepted (business.gov.au, Prepare quotes). The research found no government massage price, so set the price from your own cost and time.

instruction.heading: Do not make health claims
instruction.body: The research found no source on therapeutic or health claims for massage, and the offer must not describe a session as treating, curing or fixing a condition. Describe the session, not a result. Also avoid implying a registration or government recognition you do not hold. Better Health says massage therapists are not required to register with a government medical authority, and it lists the profession as unregulated (Better Health, massage therapist profile, undated). An offer that suggests otherwise breaches the price and claims rules in the same way as any other unsupported claim.

instruction.heading: Guarantees, fix-first and consumer law
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford. For services, a business must be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge (Consumer Victoria, last updated 13 October 2023). That source does not set a fix-window length. A written warranty is an optional extra that sits on top of the consumer guarantees, and a “no refunds” line does not override a customer’s rights for services (business.gov.au, Warranties and refunds).

instruction.heading: Session tiers, the total and packs
instruction.body: Stepped options work when each higher level adds something the client can see, such as a longer session. Jobber’s good-better-best examples, published May 2021 and updated 8 October 2024, use this pattern for trade services, but none of its examples is a massage. Show one clear total for the visit, with the travel charge on its own line, and say whether GST is included (ACCC, Setting prices: what’s allowed). Oneflare, a marketplace, estimates massage at $55 to $100 per session, and it says home visits may incur a travel fee; that page is undated, and it is a vendor estimate, not a benchmark. A pack of sessions is a prepaid service, so check the consumer rules before you sell one. The research did not state a pack discount, so do not quote one without checking it.

procedure: Write the session outcome in plain words, without any health claim, and check that you can deliver it.
Set the visit length, including set-up, clean-down and travel, and record how often you finish inside it.
List what the client must provide, such as a firm, level surface, and cut each step you can.
Add one certainty element, such as a check of the client’s wishes at the start and a written note afterwards.
Decide the fix-first approach and any warranty, and check that you can afford both.
Price the session tiers and any pack from value, then check the total against your cost, time and the marketplace range.

workedExamples.situation: A mobile massage therapist’s quote puts the travel fee into the session price, so the client cannot see what the travel adds. The client compares the total with a marketplace listing and asks why it is higher.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Rewrite the quote so the client can see the session, the set-up, the travel and the total, and explain the difference from the marketplace listing.
workedExamples.reasoning: The session price, the set-up and clean-down time, and the travel charge each sit on their own line, with one total and a GST statement. The therapist explains what the travel and the set-up cover, so the total is easy to check. The marketplace estimate is a vendor figure with no date, and it does not show whether travel is included, so the therapist does not treat it as the price to match. No price is set in this lesson.

commonErrors.error: Making a health or treatment claim you cannot support
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the session and what you do. Make no claim about a condition or a result without evidence and checked rules.

commonErrors.error: Implying a registration or government recognition you do not hold
commonErrors.prevention: State only the qualifications and registrations you hold, in the state where the session happens.

commonErrors.error: Adding a travel fee after the client has agreed to the price
commonErrors.prevention: Show the travel charge as its own line on the written quote before the visit.

commonErrors.error: Selling a pack with no written terms, expiry or cancellation rule
commonErrors.prevention: Write the pack terms and check the gift-card and prepaid rules for your state before you sell it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Massage council and state registration checks are missing. The research did not verify whether any state or territory other than Victoria requires registration for mobile massage, and the Victorian check rests on a council listing with 2017 metadata. That listing does not include massage, so treat massage as not council-registered in Victoria unless your council says otherwise, and check with your council. Do not assume that the rules for hairdressing or beauty apply to massage.

Infection control and skin-penetration rules for massage were not found in the sources read. Massage is not on the Victorian skin-penetration list, the Queensland higher-risk list or the NSW skin-penetration page read, but this has not been checked in every state. Check the rules for each state where you work before you offer any treatment that touches the skin beyond massage.

Consumer rules on prepaid services: a business must not take payment for a service it cannot supply in a reasonable time (Personal services guide, 2013, p. 10). Gift card rules apply to most cards and vouchers sold on or after 1 November 2019, with a minimum three-year expiry, and the sources read do not say whether memberships or massage packs are covered. Check the rules for your state before you sell a pack.
Business guidance only. This lesson gives no tax advice. Check the tax treatment of your income with a registered tax agent.

qualityStandard: Every offer states the session, the visit length, the client inputs, the certainty element and the risk, in writing before the visit.
The travel charge and GST status appear on the quote as separate, checkable lines.
No health or treatment claim is published without evidence and a check of the applicable rules.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or session sheet, with the date it was issued
Visit-length record, compared with the stated visit length
Pack terms, and the record of any fix-first request and its outcome
summary: A good offer promises a named session, a time frame, client inputs, certainty and a fair guarantee.
Show the travel charge and GST as visible lines, so the higher price is easy to see.
Make no health claim you cannot support, and check registration rules state by state.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a mobile offer does the customer buy?
What should a guarantee be?
options: Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new customers and friends
Something you can deliver and afford

officialReferences.covers: States that misleading statements about prices are prohibited. Publisher: ACCC.

officialReferences.title: Warranties and refunds (business.gov.au)
officialReferences.covers: Says an optional warranty sits on top of the consumer guarantees, and that a no-refunds line does not override a customer’s rights for services. Publisher: business.gov.au.

officialReferences.covers: States that massage therapists are not required to register with a government medical authority and lists registration as unregulated; says some private health funds cover massage depending on the policy and that Medicare does not.
